# **EXECUTIVE SUMMARY** {#executive-summary}

The Mekong Delta is among the regions most vulnerable to climate change in Southeast Asia. Rising sea levels, land subsidence, extreme rainfall, and abnormal tidal surges are increasing the frequency and severity of urban flooding, particularly in Can Tho City. These conditions cause traffic disruption, vehicle damage, economic losses, and significant challenges to urban mobility. Existing flood management systems remain fragmented and reactive, while conventional navigation platforms primarily optimize travel time without considering flood risks and road safety conditions.

To address this challenge, this project proposes Mekong Pathfinder, an AI-powered flood-intelligence and climate-resilient mobility platform for flood-prone urban environments. The platform integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI), Computer Vision, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and real-time crowdsourced intelligence to provide flood monitoring, hazard detection, and adaptive Safety-First Routing.

The core innovation of Mekong Pathfinder is the transformation of existing traffic cameras and community-contributed data into a distributed network of Virtual Flood Sensors. By leveraging existing municipal infrastructure and crowdsourced insights instead of deploying costly physical sensor networks, the system estimates localized flood conditions in real-time, helping commuters avoid high-risk road segments and supporting institutional flood management.

Market validation involving 445 respondents demonstrated a compelling problem-solution fit. Results showed that 79.6% of users had experienced flood-related vehicle damage, and 62.9% were willing to actively contribute mobility data, confirming the feasibility of building a scalable, crowdsourced data ecosystem.

Mekong Pathfinder adopts a B2B/B2G GovTech business model, providing a free consumer application to maximize data collection (the 'Community Overlay Layer'), while generating revenue through AI-powered analytics dashboards and flood intelligence APIs for municipal governments, logistics operators, and insurance providers. Initial deployment focuses on Can Tho City before scaling regionally, with the long-term vision of becoming the foundational mobility intelligence infrastructure for climate-resilient cities in the Mekong Delta.

# **CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION (6 \- 7 Pages)** {#chapter-1:-introduction-(6---7-pages)}

## **1.1. Idea About Products And Services** {#1.1.-idea-about-products-and-services}

Urban flooding has become one of the most significant mobility challenges in the Mekong Delta, particularly in rapidly urbanizing cities such as Can Tho. Rising sea levels, land subsidence, extreme rainfall, and abnormal tidal surges have increased both the frequency and severity of flooding, disrupting transportation systems, damaging vehicles, and negatively affecting economic activities and public safety (World Bank, 2022; Asian Development Bank \[ADB\], 2023). Recent studies further indicate that flood risks in the Mekong Delta will continue to intensify due to the combined impacts of climate change and urbanization (Wood et al., 2024). As motorbikes remain the dominant mode of transportation in the region, daily mobility is highly vulnerable to flood-related disruptions.

The convergence of increasing flood risks, expanding urban camera infrastructure, and accelerating smart-city initiatives creates a timely opportunity for deploying AI-driven mobility intelligence solutions. This environment enables innovative approaches that leverage existing infrastructure to improve urban resilience while minimizing implementation costs.

Although these developments create favorable conditions for AI-enabled mobility solutions, technological readiness alone does not guarantee effective flood-resilient navigation. The practical value of such solutions depends on their ability to address the limitations of existing navigation platforms in integrating flood intelligence, real-time environmental awareness, and safety-oriented decision support.

Figure 1 illustrates typical flood-induced mobility disruptions observed during the research team's fieldwork in Can Tho, providing real-world evidence of the transportation challenges discussed above.

**![][image2]**

#### *Figure 1\. Flood-related traffic disruptions observed during fieldwork in Binh Thuy, Can Tho (October 8, 2025).* {#figure-1.-flood-related-traffic-disruptions-observed-during-fieldwork-in-binh-thuy,-can-tho-(october-8,-2025).}

Despite the increasing severity of urban flooding, existing navigation platforms remain limited in their ability to address localized flood conditions. Applications such as Google Maps and Waze primarily optimize routes based on travel time and traffic congestion rather than environmental safety (Waze, 2026; Soul, 2026). Meanwhile, information obtained through social media and informal community channels is often fragmented, inconsistent, and difficult to verify in real time (Houston et al., 2015). As a result, commuters frequently lack reliable information when making travel decisions during flood events.

To better illustrate the functional limitations of current mobility solutions, Table 1 compares their core capabilities with those of Mekong Pathfinder.

Table 1\. Comparison of Existing Solutions and Mekong Pathfinder

| Feature | Google Maps | Waze | Social Media | Mekong Pathfinder |
| ----- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Real-time traffic navigation | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Flood depth estimation | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| AI-powered flood prediction | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Verified community flood reports | ✗ | Limited | Limited | ✓ |
| Safety-first routing based on flood risk | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Integrated rescue and repair services | Limited | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Unified flood and traffic intelligence | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |

As summarized in Table 1, existing solutions address only isolated aspects of urban mobility rather than the interconnected nature of flood-related transportation challenges. Traffic navigation, flood awareness, community reporting, and emergency response remain fragmented across multiple platforms, requiring users to synthesize information manually during time-critical situations. This fragmentation not only increases cognitive burden but also delays decision-making and may expose commuters to unsafe routes during flood events. The comparison therefore reveals a systemic gap in current mobility ecosystems, highlighting the need for an integrated platform capable of combining real-time flood monitoring, AI-driven environmental intelligence, verified community contributions, and safety-oriented navigation within a unified decision-support system.

To address this challenge, Mekong Pathfinder was developed as an AI-powered flood intelligence and climate-resilient mobility platform for flood-prone urban environments. The platform integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI), Computer Vision, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), crowdsourced intelligence, and real-time traffic information to provide flood monitoring, hazard detection, and safer route recommendations.

The core innovation of Mekong Pathfinder lies in transforming existing traffic cameras, community-contributed images, and traffic feeds into Virtual Flood Sensors. By leveraging computer vision and real-time image analysis, the system can estimate flood conditions, identify road hazards, and generate localized flood intelligence without requiring extensive deployment of dedicated sensor infrastructure (He et al., 2024; Jafari et al., 2021). This approach enables a scalable and cost-effective solution while maximizing the value of existing urban infrastructure.

Unlike conventional navigation systems that prioritize travel efficiency, Mekong Pathfinder introduces a Safety-First Routing approach that evaluates flood severity, traffic conditions, and road accessibility simultaneously when generating route recommendations. By combining AI-generated insights with community-generated reports, the platform delivers more reliable and context-aware mobility decisions for users.

Mekong Pathfinder strategically targets a multi-sided ecosystem comprising urban commuters, logistics operators, and local authorities. Initial market validation involving 245 respondents confirmed strong problem-solution fit and validated the core mechanism of the platform's data engine, with 62.9% of users expressing willingness to actively contribute community-generated flood reports. This high participation intent confirms the feasibility of utilizing a free consumer application to build a crowdsourced virtual sensor network. Can Tho City was selected as the initial pilot market due to its high flood vulnerability, overwhelming dependence on motorbikes, and proactive smart-city digital transformation initiatives.

By integrating flood intelligence, safety-oriented navigation, and community participation into a unified platform, Mekong Pathfinder aims to enhance transportation resilience, support smart city development, and contribute to safer and more climate-adaptive urban mobility across the Mekong Delta.

## **1.2. Innovativeness And Uniqueness** {#1.2.-innovativeness-and-uniqueness}

Mekong Pathfinder differentiates itself from conventional navigation and flood-monitoring solutions through four key innovations that combine artificial intelligence, community intelligence, and climate-resilient mobility design. Rather than functioning solely as a navigation application, the platform introduces a localized urban mobility intelligence ecosystem tailored to flood-prone environments in the Mekong Delta. This ecosystem adopts an interdisciplinary approach by integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI), Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Community Intelligence, and business innovation into a unified platform. AI enables automated flood detection and predictive analysis, GIS provides location-based spatial intelligence for safer route planning, Community Intelligence continuously enriches real-time situational awareness through crowdsourced contributions, while the business layer transforms these technological capabilities into sustainable services and long-term value creation. Together, these complementary disciplines reinforce one another to deliver a comprehensive and scalable mobility solution that extends beyond the capabilities of conventional navigation systems.

**AI-Powered Virtual Flood Sensors**

Unlike traditional flood-monitoring systems that rely on dedicated IoT sensors and physical water-level stations, Mekong Pathfinder utilizes existing cameras and community-contributed images as AI-powered virtual flood sensors. Through computer vision and image segmentation techniques, the system can estimate flood conditions and road accessibility in real time without requiring extensive hardware deployment (Jafari et al., 2021; Mugnozza et al., 2021). This infrastructure-light approach significantly reduces deployment costs while improving scalability across urban areas, making the solution more practical for developing cities and smart city initiatives (World Bank, 2022). Since this approach involves visual data collected from public cameras and community contributors, privacy protection is embedded into the system architecture from the design stage. Mekong Pathfinder limits data collection to operational purposes, anonymizes sensitive information whenever possible, and applies privacy safeguards to reduce the exposure of personally identifiable information in camera-based and image-based data. This Privacy-by-Design orientation strengthens the feasibility of deploying virtual flood sensors in real urban environments, where technical scalability must be balanced with public trust, data governance, and compliance with Vietnam’s Cybersecurity Law 2018 and the Personal Data Protection Law 2025 (National Assembly of Vietnam, 2018, 2025).

**![][image3]**

#### ***Figure 2\.** Existing Camera Infrastructure from Local Households* {#figure-2.-existing-camera-infrastructure-from-local-households}

**Safety-First Routing Algorithm**

While conventional navigation platforms mainly optimize routes based on travel time and congestion, Mekong Pathfinder introduces a Safety-First Routing approach that also considers flood severity, road accessibility, and environmental hazards. As illustrated in Figure 3, this dual-factor routing logic helps users avoid unsafe flooded areas rather than simply choosing the fastest route, making the platform more suitable for flood-prone urban environments (ADB, 2023).

#### **Figure 3\.** Dual-Factor Safety Routing {#figure-3.-dual-factor-safety-routing}

**Hyper-Local Emergency Support Network**

Mekong Pathfinder extends beyond navigation by integrating nearby rescue services, repair garages, volunteer response teams, and safe parking locations into a real-time support network. As illustrated in Figure 4, this hyper-local network digitizes existing community resources to provide practical assistance during flood emergencies, creating a mobility resilience function that conventional navigation platforms and public-service applications generally do not provide (Can Tho Department of Justice, 2024).

#### **Figure 4\.** Local Emergency Response Network {#figure-4.-local-emergency-response-network}

**Hybrid Data Intelligence and the “Smart 365” Strategy**

Mekong Pathfinder combines AI-generated flood intelligence with crowdsourced reports to improve data accuracy and enrich its mobility dataset (Houston et al., 2015; OECD, 2021). Because it uses location data and community participation, the platform applies user consent, anonymization, and Privacy-by-Design principles aligned with Vietnam’s data protection requirements (National Assembly of Vietnam, 2018, 2025). As shown in Figure 5, the Smart 365 strategy maintains year-round value through hazard alerts, road-safety notifications, and mobility assistance.

## **1.3. Value Proposition** {#1.3.-value-proposition}

Mekong Pathfinder creates value by addressing a clear gap in urban mobility systems in flood-prone environments: conventional navigation platforms primarily optimize for speed and traffic efficiency, but provide limited support for flood-risk awareness, road safety, and context-specific mobility decisions. This gap is particularly significant in the Mekong Delta, where motorbikes remain the dominant mode of daily transportation and flood-related disruptions directly affect travel reliability, vehicle safety, and local economic activity. Market validation further confirms the urgency of this problem, as most surveyed users had experienced flooding during travel, while a substantial proportion had encountered vehicle damage caused by flooding or traffic conditions. Mekong Pathfinder responds to this need by transforming fragmented environmental signals from cameras, community reports, GIS data, and traffic information into timely, actionable, and safety-oriented mobility intelligence.

For individual users, especially motorbike commuters in Can Tho and other flood-prone urban areas, the platform helps reduce exposure to flooded roads, vehicle damage, travel delays, and unsafe route choices. Rather than requiring users to manually compare information from maps, social media posts, informal warnings, and personal experience, Mekong Pathfinder provides real-time flood visualization and route recommendations based on flood severity, traffic conditions, and road accessibility. This value is closely aligned with user behavior identified in market validation, where many respondents expressed frustration that existing navigation tools do not show flood depth, and a large majority were willing to take a longer route if it helped avoid engine failure. The integration of emergency support points, including repair garages, rescue services, and safe parking locations, further strengthens the platform’s practical value during flood-related mobility disruptions.

For businesses such as logistics operators, delivery services, and ride-hailing companies, Mekong Pathfinder supports operational continuity in adverse weather conditions. Real-time flood intelligence can help these organizations improve route planning, reduce the likelihood of delivery delays, limit vehicle-related risks, and maintain service reliability when road networks are disrupted. This value is especially relevant for businesses whose performance depends on predictable mobility, timely delivery, and efficient fleet coordination in flood-prone cities. Rather than positioning the platform only as a consumer navigation application, Mekong Pathfinder therefore creates business value by converting localized flood and traffic data into operational intelligence for mobility-dependent enterprises (Asian Development Bank, 2023).

For government agencies and smart city stakeholders, Mekong Pathfinder provides a practical approach to urban flood monitoring and mobility management. By leveraging existing camera infrastructure, GIS layers, and community-generated reports instead of relying solely on dedicated physical sensor networks, the platform can support real-time situational awareness at lower infrastructure intensity. This capability can assist early warning, emergency coordination, infrastructure planning, and evidence-based urban governance, particularly in cities that face recurring flood-related mobility disruptions. In this sense, Mekong Pathfinder functions not only as a navigation tool but also as a GovTech and smart-city support system for climate-resilient urban management (World Bank, 2023).

Beyond its immediate functional benefits, Mekong Pathfinder creates long-term strategic value through its Hybrid Data Intelligence model. By combining AI-generated insights with crowdsourced reports, the platform can gradually improve local data accuracy while building a proprietary dataset on flood conditions, mobility behavior, road accessibility, and user-reported incidents. The defensibility of this data asset does not come merely from data ownership, but from its hyperlocal nature, repeated validation, community participation, and relevance to motorbike-dominant mobility in the Mekong Delta. Over time, this accumulated intelligence is expected to improve prediction quality, strengthen route recommendations, support institutional decision-making, and create a localized advantage that general navigation platforms may find difficult to replicate without comparable field data, community trust, and regional partnerships. Through this combination of user safety, business continuity, public-sector intelligence, and data-driven scalability, Mekong Pathfinder offers a value proposition that is socially meaningful, operationally practical, and commercially viable for climate-resilient mobility across the Mekong Delta.

## **1.4. Technology Touch** {#1.4.-technology-touch}

Mekong Pathfinder is designed as an AI-first smart mobility ecosystem that converts heterogeneous urban data into real-time flood-aware mobility intelligence. While the previous sections explain the platform’s innovation and value proposition, this section focuses on the technical mechanism through which data is collected, processed, validated, and transformed into actionable decisions. The platform integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI), Computer Vision, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), crowdsourced intelligence, routing algorithms, and cloud-native infrastructure to support safer navigation and urban flood monitoring in flood-prone environments. Its technological design is guided by three core requirements: real-time responsiveness, low-infrastructure deployment, and practical scalability for resource-constrained cities in the Mekong Delta.

The system follows an end-to-end AI processing pipeline, as shown in Figure 6\. Visual inputs from public traffic cameras, residential security cameras, and community-contributed images are first collected and preprocessed to improve visibility, filter low-quality frames, and normalize lighting conditions. These inputs are then processed by the AI vision module to perform water-area segmentation, vehicle detection, and traffic-state estimation. The resulting flood and traffic indicators are integrated with GIS road-network data, community reports, and historical mobility patterns to generate flood-aware route recommendations and user alerts. This pipeline allows Mekong Pathfinder to transform raw visual and community data into operational mobility intelligence rather than treating flood detection, traffic monitoring, and routing as separate technical functions.

![][image4]

Figure 6\. Proposed AI Processing Pipeline

At the core of this pipeline is the AI-Powered Virtual Flood Sensor framework. As illustrated in Figure 7, the platform repurposes existing camera infrastructure as a distributed environmental sensing layer, reducing dependence on newly deployed physical water-level sensors. Computer vision models analyze CCTV frames and user-submitted images to identify flooded road surfaces, estimate water coverage, and assess road accessibility. The technical direction prioritizes a YOLOv11-seg-based approach because it supports object detection and segmentation within a unified inference process, which is suitable for real-time CCTV analysis. In this design, vehicle detection provides spatial references such as wheel position and ground-contact points, while water segmentation identifies flooded areas in the scene. Alternative segmentation architectures such as U-Net may be used as benchmarking baselines, but YOLOv11-seg is more aligned with the project’s need for lightweight and real-time deployment.

![][image5]

Figure 7\. AI Vision \- “Virtual Flood Sensors” Utilizing Existing Camera Infrastructure

Flood severity estimation is performed through the combination of segmentation and spatial calibration. Figure 8 illustrates how water-level recognition and traffic-flow assessment are connected within the same technical workflow. After the water region is detected, the system estimates flood level by referencing visible environmental objects such as curbs, lane markings, sidewalks, and vehicle wheels. To reduce reliance on physical sensors, the platform applies camera-based calibration principles, including perspective estimation and reference-object scaling, to approximate flood depth from image data. In more advanced deployment scenarios, this mechanism can be strengthened through a dual-mode calibration approach, using dynamic calibration when vehicles or road objects are visible and static region-of-interest calibration when the scene contains fewer reference objects. This design is important for urban CCTV environments because camera angle, object availability, lighting, and visibility conditions vary significantly across locations.

![][image6]

Figure 8\. Real-Time Water Level Recognition and Traffic Flow Assessment System

For traffic analysis, Mekong Pathfinder emphasizes macro-level traffic assessment rather than depending entirely on continuous object tracking. Conventional tracking methods may become unstable under low-frame-rate CCTV streams, occlusion, heavy rain, and night-time conditions. Therefore, the system combines vehicle detection with indicators such as vehicle density, road occupancy, and stagnation patterns within a defined region of interest. This approach is more suitable for practical urban monitoring because it evaluates the overall traffic state rather than requiring the system to maintain the identity of each individual vehicle. The resulting traffic indicators are then combined with flood severity and road accessibility data to support Safety-First Routing.

The routing engine is designed around weighted graph-based routing logic. As shown in Figure 9, route selection is determined not only by travel speed or distance, but also by the interaction between flood conditions and traffic conditions. Each road segment is assigned dynamic risk weights based on flood depth, congestion level, road accessibility, incident reports, and historical disruption patterns. Existing routing engines such as GraphHopper or similar GIS-based tools can be integrated with custom flood-risk weighting to generate safety-oriented route recommendations. Although learning-based graph models may be explored in future research, the current system prioritizes interpretable graph-weighting mechanisms because they are easier to validate, explain, and deploy in public-sector contexts.

![][image7]

Figure 9\. Dual-Factor “Safety-First Routing”

To improve reliability, Mekong Pathfinder applies a Hybrid Data Intelligence model that cross-validates AI-generated observations with crowdsourced reports. As demonstrated in Figure 10, user reports on flooding, traffic incidents, road hazards, and accessibility conditions complement AI predictions and GIS context. This hybrid validation mechanism is necessary because computer vision outputs may become uncertain under difficult weather or lighting conditions, while community reports may be delayed, incomplete, or inconsistent. By comparing multiple data sources, the platform can improve confidence scoring, reduce inaccurate alerts, and gradually build a hyperlocal dataset for model refinement and future predictive analytics.

![][image8]

Figure 10\. Hybrid Data System \- Combining AI and Community Power

Beyond flood detection and routing, Mekong Pathfinder also digitizes local emergency support resources. As illustrated in Figure 11, the platform connects users with nearby repair garages, rescue teams, towing services, and safe parking locations during severe flooding events. This function extends the system from a navigation tool into a mobility resilience platform by linking flood intelligence with practical emergency assistance. The integration of these local services improves response accessibility and strengthens community-based resilience during flood-related mobility disruptions.

![][image9]

Figure 11\. Digitization of the Local Emergency Response Network

The system also recognizes the practical limitations of computer vision in real-world flood monitoring. CCTV-based detection can be affected by heavy rain, low-light conditions, glare, water reflection, occlusion, camera vibration, fog, compression artifacts, and inconsistent camera angles. Night-time environments may reduce segmentation accuracy, while turbid floodwater may appear visually similar to road surfaces under certain lighting conditions. These limitations are addressed through preprocessing techniques such as image enhancement, frame quality filtering, and low-light normalization, combined with data augmentation, transfer learning, and training data collected under diverse weather and lighting conditions. When uncertainty remains high, the system should lower the confidence score, request community validation, or rely on nearby verified data sources instead of issuing overly confident alerts.

To address seasonal user churn, Mekong Pathfinder adopts a Smart 365 strategy that extends platform value beyond the flood season. As shown in Figure 12, the platform remains useful during normal weather conditions by providing daily mobility assistance, including hazard alerts, accident blackspot notifications, traffic sign recognition, and AI-generated traffic broadcasts. This year-round utility helps maintain user engagement, supports continuous data generation, and strengthens long-term ecosystem growth (Deloitte, 2023).

![][image10]

Figure 12\. Smart 365 Strategy and AI Traffic Radio

Beyond AI processing, Mekong Pathfinder is supported by a microservice and edge-to-cloud architecture. As illustrated in Figure 13, the system is organized into independent but interconnected services, including AI Flood Detection, Routing Engine, Community Verification, Emergency Support, Notification Service, User Service, and Administrative Dashboard. Edge processing supports low-latency image analysis near camera sources, while cloud infrastructure handles data storage, model updates, large-scale analytics, synchronization, and dashboard services. This architecture improves maintainability, allows critical services to scale independently, and reduces the risk that a failure in one component will disrupt the entire platform.

![][image11]

Figure 13\. Microservice and Edge-to-Cloud Processing Architecture

The mobile and dashboard layers translate technical outputs into practical decision-support interfaces. On the mobile application, users receive flood alerts, route recommendations, hazard notifications, camera-based status updates, and emergency support suggestions. On the administrative dashboard, authorities and operators can monitor flood-prone locations, review verified reports, observe traffic conditions, and coordinate response activities. This layered design ensures that AI outputs are not only processed technically but also converted into usable information for both citizens and institutional stakeholders.

Because the platform processes geolocation data, community reports, and visual information from cameras, privacy and cybersecurity are treated as technical design requirements. User location is collected only with consent and anonymized before being used for traffic analytics. Communication between mobile clients, edge nodes, and cloud services is protected through encrypted transmission. Community-submitted images and camera-derived data should be processed to minimize exposure of identifiable personal information, such as faces, license plates, and private property details, whenever applicable. Access to operational datasets is restricted through authentication and role-based authorization. These measures support compliance with Vietnam’s Cybersecurity Law 2018 and the Personal Data Protection Law 2025 while strengthening the platform’s readiness for public-sector and smart-city deployment (National Assembly of Vietnam, 2018, 2025).

Through the integration of AI-based visual sensing, spatial calibration, macro-level traffic analysis, graph-based routing, hybrid data validation, emergency support integration, Smart 365 engagement mechanisms, and scalable cloud-native infrastructure, Mekong Pathfinder establishes a technically feasible foundation for flood-aware mobility intelligence in the Mekong Delta. Its technological strength does not depend on a single model or isolated feature, but on the coordinated interaction between computer vision, GIS, community data, routing logic, secure architecture, and real-world service integration. This integrated design enables the platform to support real-time mobility decisions while remaining scalable, adaptable, and suitable for future expansion across flood-prone urban environments.

## **1.5. Project Impacts** {#1.5.-project-impacts}

Mekong Pathfinder goes beyond a conventional navigation application by functioning as a climate-resilient urban mobility intelligence platform for the Mekong Delta. Its expected impact lies in improving how flood-related mobility risks are detected, reported, verified, and translated into safer travel decisions. The project’s impact logic is therefore practical and measurable: real-time flood intelligence improves user awareness, better awareness supports safer route choices, safer route choices reduce exposure to high-risk flooded roads, and aggregated mobility data supports more coordinated urban management.

From an economic perspective, Mekong Pathfinder addresses the recurring financial burden caused by flood-related vehicle damage, travel disruption, and productivity loss. Urban flooding does not only delay movement; it also increases the risk of engine failure, unnecessary detours, fuel waste, and lost working time. By providing real-time flood alerts and Safety-First Routing, the platform is expected to reduce users’ exposure to deeply flooded or highly congested road segments. During the pilot stage, this impact should be measured through indicators such as avoided high-risk flooded routes, reduced travel delay on monitored corridors, fewer flood-related vehicle incidents reported by active users, and lower unnecessary detours. Conservative pilot targets may include reducing avoidable flood-related travel delay by 10-20% on monitored routes and reducing exposure to high-risk flooded segments by 10-15% among active users. These figures should be interpreted as evaluation targets rather than confirmed outcomes, providing a realistic basis for assessing whether flood-aware mobility intelligence can generate measurable economic value.

From a social perspective, the platform contributes to public safety and community resilience by improving access to timely hazard information and nearby support services during flood events. Instead of relying only on fragmented social media posts, informal warnings, or personal experience, users can access a structured information environment that combines AI-generated observations, community reports, and location-based emergency support. This participatory model enables citizens to contribute flood reports while also benefiting from verified information submitted by others. In the pilot phase, social impact can be assessed through the number of verified community reports, the response rate to hazard alerts, the number of users accessing repair or rescue points, and user confidence in making travel decisions during flood conditions (Houston et al., 2015).

At the institutional level, Mekong Pathfinder supports smart-city and digital-transformation initiatives by converting existing camera infrastructure, GIS data, and community-generated reports into actionable urban intelligence. For local authorities, this creates an opportunity to shift from fragmented and reactive observation toward more evidence-based flood monitoring and traffic coordination. By using existing cameras and community inputs rather than relying solely on large-scale deployment of physical sensors, the platform provides a lower-infrastructure pathway for improving situational awareness. Relevant institutional indicators include the number of monitored flood-prone locations, the volume of verified reports available to authorities, the time required to identify recurring flood hotspots, and the extent to which dashboard insights support emergency coordination or infrastructure planning (World Bank, 2023; Deloitte, 2023).

Environmentally, Mekong Pathfinder contributes to climate adaptation by helping citizens and authorities respond more intelligently to increasingly frequent urban flooding. The platform does not directly eliminate flooding, but it improves adaptive capacity by enabling risk-aware travel behavior, supporting data-driven planning, and creating a localized evidence base for flood-prone road segments. Its contribution to SDG 9 lies in the use of digital infrastructure and AI-enabled sensing; its contribution to SDG 11 lies in supporting safer and more resilient urban mobility; and its contribution to SDG 13 lies in strengthening climate adaptation through real-time flood intelligence and community-based reporting. If future pilots confirm reductions in unnecessary detours or congestion-related delays, the platform may also contribute indirectly to lower fuel waste and associated emissions (World Bank, 2022; UNDP, 2024).

Overall, Mekong Pathfinder’s impact should be evaluated through both user-level and system-level indicators. At the user level, the most relevant measures include avoided exposure to flooded routes, reduced mobility uncertainty, faster access to emergency support, and improved confidence in route decisions. At the system level, the key measures include verified flood reports, monitored hotspots, improved data availability for local authorities, and the gradual accumulation of hyperlocal flood-mobility intelligence. Through this combination of economic value, public safety, institutional usefulness, and climate-adaptation relevance, Mekong Pathfinder provides a practical foundation for safer and more sustainable urban transportation in Vietnam.

## **1.6. Project’s Main Result At The End Of EXE201** {#1.6.-project’s-main-result-at-the-end-of-exe201}

By the end of the EXE201 phase, Mekong Pathfinder successfully evolved from a conceptual smart mobility solution into a validated startup prototype with initial real-world deployment activities. The project achieved key milestones in technology development, market validation, pilot implementation, and commercialization readiness.

From a technical perspective, the team successfully developed the first Minimum Viable Product (MVP), integrating core functionalities such as flood-aware navigation, community reporting, emergency support services, and the foundational architecture for AI-powered flood intelligence. The project also validated the feasibility of the Virtual Flood Sensor concept and Safety-First Routing approach using existing camera infrastructure rather than costly dedicated sensor networks.

To support development and pilot activities, the project received a 50 million VND startup development grant from FPT University Can Tho campus. This funding enabled the team to build the MVP, conduct field research, and initiate real-world testing.

Market validation involving 245 respondents confirmed a strong demand for a flood-resilient mobility solution. The results highlighted high user engagement potential: 62.9% of respondents expressed willingness to actively contribute real-time flood reports and mobility data, directly validating the feasibility of the project's 'Community Overlay Layer' and crowdsourced data engine. This widespread willingness to participate in a collaborative data ecosystem confirms that Mekong Pathfinder can effectively leverage its user base to enhance urban resilience, thereby building a defensible proprietary dataset for its institutional B2B and B2G service offerings.

Beyond survey validation, the first MVP pilot attracted 302 early users who actively tested the platform and provided valuable feedback on user experience, routing preferences, and feature improvements. In parallel, the team began installing and integrating pilot camera locations to evaluate the feasibility of AI-based flood monitoring under real-world conditions.

Overall, EXE201 transformed Mekong Pathfinder from an initial concept into a validated and executable startup initiative. Through MVP development, grant funding acquisition, user validation, and pilot deployment, the project established a strong foundation for future commercialization and regional expansion.

Mekong Pathfinder is a startup project developed at FPT University Can Tho Campus as part of the Entrepreneurial Experience (EXE) program. The project aims to develop an AI-powered flood intelligence and climate-resilient mobility platform that supports safer navigation and adaptive transportation in the Mekong Delta.  The project is supported by an advisory board consisting of academic experts who provide strategic, technical, and business guidance throughout the development process.

# **CHAPTER 2: BUSINESS PERFORMANCE (10 \- 15 Pages)** {#chapter-2:-business-performance-(10---15-pages)}

## **2.1. Market Potential, Market Trend, and Product Commercialization Analysis** {#2.1.-market-potential,-market-trend,-and-product-commercialization-analysis}

### **2.1.1. Market Potential** {#2.1.1.-market-potential}

The Mekong Delta is one of Vietnam’s most economically vital yet climate-vulnerable regions, contributing approximately 12.4% of national GDP while supporting over 17 million people (World Bank, 2025). Persistent urban flooding and tidal inundation continue to disrupt transportation, causing substantial economic losses. In Can Tho City alone, annual economic damage from chronic flooding was previously estimated at nearly USD 300 million (World Bank, 2025).

To quantify the opportunity for Mekong Pathfinder, a three-level market sizing framework was applied:

* **Total Addressable Market (TAM)**: The broader smart city and climate technology market in Vietnam is projected to reach USD 800 million to 1.2 billion during 2026-2030 (IMARC Group, 2025). However, Mekong Pathfinder specifically targets the **urban flood management and climate-resilient mobility** segment.  Within this narrower scope, the relevant TAM for flood intelligence, early warning systems, and safety-first routing solutions is estimated at **USD 50-80 million** over the same period.

* **Serviceable Addressable Market (SAM)**: Mekong Pathfinder focuses on the 13 provinces of the Mekong Delta, where flood-related mobility challenges are most severe. This region benefits from increasing public investment in smart city development, disaster risk reduction, and climate adaptation programs, supported by national policies and international partners such as the World Bank, ADB, and GIZ. Provincial budgets for digital transformation and flood management have grown steadily, creating demand for cost-effective technology solutions among municipal governments, transportation departments, disaster management agencies, and logistics operators. Based on these investment trends, the SAM for Mekong Pathfinder in the Mekong Delta is estimated at **USD 25-40 million** during 2026-2030.

* **Serviceable Obtainable Market (SOM)**: As an early-stage startup operating in the GovTech sector, Mekong Pathfinder adopts a conservative “land-and-expand” strategy, prioritizing pilot success and institutional trust-building over rapid market capture.

Table 1\. Projected SOM for Mekong Pathfinder (Base Case)

**Validation of Customer Demand**

Primary research involving 245 respondents in Can Tho confirms strong demand for flood-resilient mobility solutions. Approximately 89.8% of respondents experienced flooding during travel, 91.4% encountered traffic congestion, and 91.9% reported that these issues significantly affect their daily lives. The survey also aligns closely with Mekong Pathfinder’s target users, with 93.1% relying on motorbikes as their primary mode of transportation. Market acceptance indicators are encouraging: 54.3% expressed willingness to pay for premium features, 62.9% were willing to contribute crowdsourced reports, and 86.1% were open to sharing anonymized location data under certain conditions, supporting the development of a sustainable data ecosystem. 

### **2.1.2. Market Trends** {#2.1.2.-market-trends}

Mekong Pathfinder benefits from three converging market trends that strongly support its value proposition and business model.

**Rising Investment in Climate Resilience and Smart City Development**

National strategies such as Resolution 52-NQ/TW (Politburo, 2019\) and Resolution 13-NQ/TW (Politburo, 2022\) have driven increased funding for climate adaptation and digital urban infrastructure in the Mekong Delta. Local governments are shifting from purely infrastructural flood control toward integrated technology solutions for proactive risk management.

**Transition from Hardware to Software-Driven Urban Intelligence**

Traditional flood monitoring systems that rely on dedicated IoT sensors incur high capital and maintenance costs. Advances in AI, computer vision, and open geospatial data now enable software-based alternatives. Mekong Pathfinder directly leverages this shift through its “Virtual Flood Sensor” architecture, which utilizes existing municipal cameras and satellite data to deliver scalable, low-cost flood intelligence.

**Rise of Hyperlocal Urban Intelligence Demand**

While global navigation platforms optimize primarily for speed and distance, cities and commuters in flood-prone regions increasingly require specialized, hyperlocal environmental intelligence, including real-time flood depth, road accessibility, and dynamic risk assessment. This gap creates strong demand for dedicated safety-first mobility platforms. Mekong Pathfinder is well-positioned to address this need by combining localized data with practical routing intelligence tailored to motorbike-dominant traffic in the Mekong Delta.

### **2.1.3. Product Commercialization** {#2.1.3.-product-commercialization}

Mekong Pathfinder pursues a phased commercialization strategy tailored to the realities of the GovTech and ClimateTech sectors, where long sales cycles and building institutional trust are critical. The commercialization journey begins with technical validation and pilot deployments in Can Tho City during 2026, focusing on demonstrating product effectiveness and establishing early government partnerships. From 2027 to 2028, the platform will expand across the Mekong Delta while transitioning toward recurring revenue through SaaS subscriptions and data services. By 2029-2030, Mekong Pathfinder aims to scale into a regional urban resilience intelligence platform, leveraging broader API integrations and strategic partnerships to support flood management, mobility planning, and climate adaptation initiatives across multiple provinces.

**Revenue Model and Unit Economics**

The startup uses a hybrid model with a free B2C application to drive data accumulation and institutional revenue as the primary monetization engine.

**Table 2\. Key Unit Economics (Estimated)**

Early funding will come primarily from non-dilutive sources (grants, competitions, university support, and climate funds). As the platform demonstrates value, revenue will shift toward high-margin, recurring institutional contracts. The core long-term asset remains the proprietary hyperlocal flood and mobility dataset, which strengthens the platform’s competitive moat over time.

## **2.2. Competitor Analysis** {#2.2.-competitor-analysis}

The navigation, weather alert, and urban mobility market in Vietnam is competitive. However, a clear gap remains in hyper-local, real-time flood intelligence solutions tailored to the Mekong Delta region. This section analyzes key competitors across four categories: Global Navigation Platforms, IoT-based City Applications, Local Administrative Apps, and Social Media Communities to identify Mekong Pathfinder’s competitive positioning and moat.

### **2.2.1. Market Share And Key Competitors** {#2.2.1.-market-share-and-key-competitors}

**Market Share Overview**

In Vietnam's general navigation and mobility market, global platforms dominate. Google Maps and Waze are among the most widely used navigation platforms in Vietnam, particularly for personal mobility and route planning. Grab, through its super-app ecosystem, commands significant influence in ride-hailing and delivery routing. In contrast, specialized flood monitoring solutions remain fragmented. Local administrative platforms such as CanThoSmart have a strong presence within specific cities but limited regional coverage and features. Social media groups (Facebook and Zalo) serve as the primary informal source of flood information for many residents in the Mekong Delta, despite lacking structured data and routing capabilities. Mekong Pathfinder currently operates as an emerging niche player focusing exclusively on flood-resilient mobility.

**Porter’s Five Forces Analysis**

To assess the structural attractiveness of the flood intelligence and resilient mobility segment, Porter’s Five Forces framework is applied.

Table 2\. Porter’s Five Forces Analysis for Mekong Pathfinder

![][image14]

The analysis indicates a **Moderate-to-High** overall competitive force. The most significant challenges stem from substitutes such as Google Maps and community-based social media groups. However, the absence of specialized flood-aware routing and hyperlocal flood intelligence reduces the intensity of direct competition. 

**Competitor Matrix and Competitive Gap Analysis**

Table 3\. Competitive Gap Analysis

**![][image15]**

The gap analysis demonstrates that while incumbents excel in general navigation or basic information dissemination, none currently offers a comprehensive, integrated solution combining AI Virtual Flood Sensors, safety-first routing, and hybrid data validation tailored for the Mekong Delta. This positioning allows Mekong Pathfinder to compete through specialization rather than scale, focusing on a problem that is underserved by both global navigation providers and local information platforms.

### **2.2.2. Success Factors And Competitive Advantages** {#2.2.2.-success-factors-and-competitive-advantages}

Mekong Pathfinder’s ability to compete effectively stems from several interconnected strengths that align with the opportunities and threats identified in the PESTLE and SWOT analyses.

**Hyperlocal Knowledge and Founder-Market Fit**

The founding team consists of members who are native to or have long-term residency in the Mekong Delta. Their direct, lived experience navigating flood-prone urban environments provides critical contextual understanding of local topography, traffic patterns, and seasonal flooding behaviors. This founder-market fit enables more accurate problem definition and faster iteration compared to teams based in major cities.

**CAPEX-Light Virtual Flood Sensors**

A core technical advantage is the platform’s ability to transform existing municipal cameras into intelligent “Virtual Flood Sensors” using computer vision and AI. This software-first approach significantly reduces infrastructure costs compared to traditional IoT deployments, making it more attractive to budget-constrained local governments.

**Emerging Data Advantage**

Through continuous operation and crowdsourced reporting, Mekong Pathfinder is building a growing repository of hyperlocal flood and mobility data. While not yet a fully defensible moat, this emerging data advantage is expected to strengthen over time as the volume and quality of localized, ground-truth data increase.

**Safety-First Routing Architecture**

Unlike conventional navigation tools that primarily optimize for speed or distance, Mekong Pathfinder employs a specialized routing algorithm that prioritizes flood-risk avoidance, road accessibility, and user safety, which is particularly relevant to the region’s predominant motorbike traffic.

**Institutional Backing and Ecosystem Networks**

Support from FPT University Can Tho campus provides technical resources, academic credibility, and introductions to local government stakeholders. These relationships facilitate pilot deployments and help navigate the complex B2G procurement environment.

### **2.2.3. Positioning And Differentiation Strategies** {#2.2.3.-positioning-and-differentiation-strategies}

Mekong Pathfinder adopts a focused differentiation strategy by positioning itself as a specialized **ClimateTech and GovTech solution provider** for flood-resilient urban mobility in the Mekong Delta, rather than a general navigation application.

**Strategic Anti-Positioning**

The platform deliberately avoids direct competition with global navigation leaders (Google Maps, Grab) in the broad mobility market. Instead, it concentrates on the critical gap of urban mobility safety during flooding events, an area where existing solutions fall short in depth and localization. 

**Why Incumbents Cannot Easily Replicate**

Although large technology companies possess the technical capability to replicate individual features, flood-resilient mobility in the Mekong Delta represents a relatively narrow market segment. As a result, sustained investment in localized data collection, regional partnerships, and field validation may not align with the strategic priorities of larger platforms.

**Solution Provider Identity**

Mekong Pathfinder differentiates itself commercially by operating primarily as a B2B/B2G solution provider rather than a consumer-only application. By delivering enterprise-grade dashboards, smart mobility APIs, and flood intelligence services, the platform aligns with the procurement preferences and long-term planning needs of municipal governments and logistics operators, thereby enhancing customer stickiness and revenue predictability.

## **2.3. PESTLE Analysis \- Macro Environment Analysis** {#2.3.-pestle-analysis---macro-environment-analysis}

**![][image16]**

### **2.3.1. Political Factors** {#2.3.1.-political-factors}

The Vietnamese government has shown a strong commitment to digital transformation and climate change adaptation through Resolution 52-NQ/TW (2019) and Resolution 13-NQ/TW (2022). These policies create a supportive environment for GovTech solutions like Mekong Pathfinder, especially in the Mekong Delta, where multiple provinces have approved Smart City initiatives. However, lengthy project approval cycles (9-18 months) and complex administrative procedures remain major challenges. This aligns with the high Buyer Power identified in Porter’s Five Forces analysis (2.2.1). Although public procurement processes often involve lengthy approval cycles and multiple stakeholders, government support for digital transformation creates favorable conditions for pilot projects and Public-Private Partnerships (PPP). Therefore, Mekong Pathfinder will prioritize small-scale pilots and institutional partnerships to build trust before pursuing larger government contracts.

### **2.3.2. Economic Factors** {#2.3.2.-economic-factors}

The Mekong Delta contributes approximately 12.4% of Vietnam’s GDP but suffers significant economic losses from flooding, estimated at hundreds of millions of USD annually in Can Tho alone (World Bank, 2025). This situation directly supports the TAM/SAM projections for Mekong Pathfinder (2.1.1) by generating clear demand for risk-reduction solutions in logistics and transportation. Although local technology budgets remain limited, growing ODA and climate finance programs supported by organizations such as the World Bank, ADB, and GIZ create opportunities for innovative climate adaptation solutions. Therefore, Mekong Pathfinder adopts a software-first, low-CAPEX deployment model that minimizes infrastructure costs while remaining financially accessible to local governments and public agencies.

### **2.3.3. Social Factors** {#2.3.3.-social-factors}

Public awareness of flood risks has increased significantly, with 73% of survey respondents (n=245) considering real-time flood alerts and safe routing highly necessary. A young population and high smartphone penetration (\>85%) favor technology adoption. However, reliance on Facebook and Zalo groups for free information remains strong, explaining the high Threat of Substitutes in the competitive analysis (2.2.1). This reality reinforces the project’s strategic focus on B2G/B2B revenue models while using the consumer application primarily as a channel for data acquisition and community engagement. By combining crowdsourced reports with institutional partnerships, Mekong Pathfinder can transform informal community information into structured and actionable mobility intelligence.

### **2.3.4. Technological Factors** {#2.3.4.-technological-factors}

Advancements in AI, computer vision, Sentinel satellite data, and 5G create favorable conditions for the Virtual Flood Sensor architecture, a key differentiator against traditional IoT solutions (2.2.2). Advancements in AI, computer vision, Sentinel satellite data, cloud computing, and expanding 5G infrastructure create favorable conditions for the Virtual Flood Sensor architecture, a key differentiator compared to traditional IoT-based monitoring systems (2.2.2). However, challenges remain, including inconsistent camera coverage, fragmented public data sources, and limited availability of specialized AI talent. To address these constraints, Mekong Pathfinder adopts a hybrid, multi-source approach that combines camera feeds, crowdsourced reports, satellite imagery, and geospatial data, and leverages academic partnerships to support future AI development.

### **2.3.5. Environmental Factors** {#2.3.5.-environmental-factors}

Environmental factors represent the primary driver behind Mekong Pathfinder’s value proposition. The Mekong Delta is among the regions most vulnerable to climate change, facing rising sea levels, increasingly intense rainfall, tidal flooding, and significant land subsidence in several urban areas. Combined, these factors are expected to increase both the frequency and severity of mobility disruptions over the coming decades. As flooding becomes more unpredictable, demand for real-time flood intelligence, early warning systems, and resilient mobility solutions is likely to grow. This reinforces the market opportunity identified in Section 2.1.1 and strengthens Mekong Pathfinder’s positioning as a specialized platform for climate adaptation and urban resilience in the Mekong Delta.

### **2.3.6. Legal Factors** {#2.3.6.-legal-factors}

Mekong Pathfinder must comply with key regulatory frameworks, including the Law on Cybersecurity 2018, the Personal Data Protection Law 2025, and the Bidding Law 2023\. As the platform relies on location data, community-generated reports, and public camera feeds, clear policies regarding data ownership, user consent, data retention, and information security are essential. In addition, public-sector procurement regulations may contribute to longer sales cycles and higher compliance requirements for B2G contracts. Therefore, establishing strong legal governance and transparent data management practices will be critical for building institutional trust, reducing operational risks, and supporting long-term scalability.

## **2.4. SWOT Analysis \- Internal Environment Analysis** {#2.4.-swot-analysis---internal-environment-analysis}

SWOT analysis evaluates Mekong Pathfinder’s internal capabilities in the context of the macro environment (2.3) and competitive landscape (2.2).

### **2.4.1. Strengths** {#2.4.1.-strengths}

The project’s greatest strength is its strong founder-market fit, with a locally rooted team possessing deep knowledge of the Mekong Delta’s topography and flooding patterns. Combined with the CAPEX-light Virtual Flood Sensor model, this creates a clear competitive gap compared to existing solutions (2.2.1) and capitalizes on the shift toward software-driven intelligence (2.1.2). Institutional support from FPT University Can Tho further enhances pilot access and credibility.

### **2.4.2. Weaknesses** {#2.4.2.-weaknesses}

As an early-stage startup, Mekong Pathfinder faces limitations in commercialization experience, financial resources, and brand recognition. The platform is currently in an early deployment stage, and the accuracy of the Virtual Flood Sensor architecture has not yet been validated at scale across multiple provinces. These constraints increase vulnerability to strong Buyer Power from B2G clients and potential imitation by larger players (2.2.3). The current reliance on grants and competition funding in the early years further underscores the importance of securing recurring institutional revenue, as outlined in Section 2.1.3.

### **2.4.3. Opportunities** {#2.4.3.-opportunities}

Mekong Pathfinder is well-positioned to capture the SAM of USD 25-40 million (2.1.1), benefit from the rising demand for hyperlocal intelligence (2.1.2), and exploit the significant gap in flood-aware routing (2.2.1). Increasing climate finance from the World Bank and ADB, along with Smart City initiatives, offers strong potential to scale from pilots to recurring SaaS and API contracts.

### **2.4.4. Threats** {#2.4.4.-threats}

Key threats include lengthy B2G procurement cycles, shifts in local leadership priorities, and the potential entry of larger organizations, such as Grab, FPT, or Viettel, into adjacent market segments. The widespread use of free information from social media groups also represents a strong substitute (2.2.1). To mitigate these risks, Mekong Pathfinder must continuously strengthen its proprietary data assets, improve routing intelligence, and deepen institutional relationships that new entrants may struggle to replicate quickly.

## **2.5. Marketing Mix \- 4Ps** {#2.5.-marketing-mix---4ps}

### **2.5.1. Product** {#2.5.1.-product}

Mekong Pathfinder is a climate-resilient mobility platform centered on “Safety-First Routing,” powered by AI Virtual Flood Sensors and hybrid data sources. Unlike Google Maps or Grab, which optimize for speed, the platform prioritizes flood risk mitigation, directly addressing the competitive gaps identified in 2.2.1 and leveraging the trend toward hyperlocal intelligence (2.1.2). The solution adopts a dual-sided approach: a free mobile app for individual users and enterprise dashboards with APIs for B2B/B2G clients. Key functionalities include real-time flood visualization, traffic monitoring, community incident reporting, flood-aware route recommendations, traffic camera integration, and emergency support point identification. Together, these features provide practical mobility intelligence tailored to flood-prone environments. 

### **2.5.2. Price** {#2.5.2.-price}

The project employs a freemium model to accelerate user adoption and data accumulation. The B2C application is free, while revenue is generated primarily through institutional clients using a tiered pricing structure. Pilot deployments are priced at approximately VND 30-60 million per project, while annual dashboard subscriptions range from VND 50-100 million depending on deployment scale and service requirements. Additional revenue may be generated through analytics services and API integrations for enterprise partners.

### **2.5.3. Place** {#2.5.3.-place}

Distribution follows a phased geographic rollout, starting in Can Tho, the economic hub with the highest flood vulnerability (2.1.1). After successful pilots, expansion will target neighboring provinces. B2C distribution occurs through mobile application stores and digital channels. For institutional customers, market access is achieved through pilot projects, direct government engagement, Public-Private Partnerships (PPP), university-supported introductions, and participation in Smart City and climate innovation programs.

### **2.5.4. Promotion** {#2.5.4.-promotion}

Promotion strategies emphasize trust-building, community engagement, and institutional credibility. For individual users, awareness is driven through educational content on TikTok and Facebook, community campaigns, and university ambassador programs that encourage crowdsourced reporting. For B2B and B2G customers, marketing focuses on pilot demonstrations, technical whitepapers, startup competitions, Smart City forums, and direct engagement with government agencies. This dual-channel approach supports both user acquisition and long-term institutional sales while strengthening the project’s reputation within the regional innovation ecosystem.

## **2.6. Business Model \- Canvas** {#2.6.-business-model---canvas}

*Figure X. Business Model Canvas*

Figure X presents the Business Model Canvas of Mekong Pathfinder. The model highlights a hybrid B2B/B2G commercialization approach, in which municipal governments, transportation agencies, and logistics operators are the primary customer segments. A notable strength of the model is the combination of recurring institutional revenue (dashboard subscriptions, API licensing, and analytics services) and community-generated data, which continuously enhances service quality. This structure creates a reinforcing data network effect and supports long-term scalability while maintaining relatively low infrastructure costs. 

## **2.7. Minimum Viable Product Improvements** {#2.7.-minimum-viable-product-improvements}

### **2.7.1. Analyze And Evaluate The Product's Suitability By The End Of EXE201** {#2.7.1.-analyze-and-evaluate-the-product's-suitability-by-the-end-of-exe201}

By the end of the EXE201 phase, Mekong Pathfinder had developed a functional Minimum Viable Product (MVP) to address two major mobility challenges in the Mekong Delta: urban flooding and traffic congestion. Following Lean Startup principles (Ries, 2011), the project prioritized validating user problems and solution assumptions before expanding into more complex smart-city functionalities.

The MVP was informed by primary research involving 245 respondents in Can Tho. Survey results indicated that over 90% of participants relied on motorbikes for daily transportation, while approximately 74% reported frequent disruptions due to flooding and traffic conditions. Based on these findings, the MVP concentrated on four core functions: real-time flood visualization, traffic monitoring, community incident reporting, and safety-oriented route guidance.

From a product perspective, the MVP demonstrated strong alignment with user needs. Respondents consistently prioritized real-time hazard information, traffic camera visibility, and route safety over traditional shortest-path navigation. Consequently, Mekong Pathfinder adopted a “safety-first mobility” positioning, introducing a routing approach that considers both flood risk and traffic conditions when recommending routes.

Technically, the MVP validated the feasibility of integrating GIS visualization, crowdsourced reporting, and cloud-based data processing within a unified platform. The system also established the foundation for future AI-powered flood detection using existing public traffic cameras, reducing reliance on expensive IoT infrastructure.

Commercially, the MVP generated encouraging validation signals for the platform’s 'Community Overlay Layer.' Rather than relying on consumer-side subscriptions, the validation focused on community engagement potential: 62.9% of respondents expressed willingness to actively contribute verified flood and mobility reports. This high participation intent confirms the feasibility of a crowdsourced data engine, establishing a foundation where the user base functions as a distributed sensor network. This data-contribution model allows Mekong Pathfinder to aggregate hyperlocal intelligence, which serves as the primary asset for future B2B/B2G commercialization.

However, several limitations remained, including the absence of predictive flood analytics, automated report verification, offline navigation capabilities, and institutional integrations. Therefore, although full Product-Market Fit had not yet been achieved, the EXE201 MVP successfully demonstrated strong Problem-Solution Fit, technical feasibility, and initial market acceptance, providing a solid foundation for further development in EXE402. 

### **2.7.2. Product Improvement Plan** {#2.7.2.-product-improvement-plan}

Based on the evaluation of the EXE201 MVP, improvement priorities were selected using an Impact-Feasibility approach to focus development efforts on initiatives that could deliver the highest user value while remaining technically achievable within the EXE402 phase. 

The first priority was improving user experience. Because users often access the platform during adverse weather conditions, the interface was redesigned to reduce cognitive load through simplified navigation, one-tap incident reporting, and clearer flood-risk visualization. These improvements aimed to increase reporting participation and improve emergency usability.

The second priority focused on data quality and trustworthiness. To address misinformation and duplicate reports, a hybrid validation architecture was introduced. This approach combines community-generated reports with AI analysis of traffic camera data, historical flood patterns, and geospatial validation techniques. The objective was to improve data accuracy while maintaining a low-cost deployment model.

The third priority involved upgrading the routing engine. Rather than relying solely on distance or travel time, the new routing framework incorporates flood depth, road accessibility, congestion levels, and historical disruption data to calculate safer routes for motorbike users.

Finally, the backend architecture was restructured into a modular, service-oriented design to improve scalability and maintainability, and to enable future integration with government systems, weather services, and enterprise partners.

The EXE402 phase successfully transformed Mekong Pathfinder from a proof-of-concept prototype into an early-stage deployable platform. Improvements were achieved across usability, routing intelligence, system architecture, and data integration readiness. Year 2 concentrates on regional expansion and revenue generation, while Year 3 aims to establish Mekong Pathfinder as a regional mobility resilience platform. # **CHAPTER 3: RISK IDENTIFICATION (10 \- 15 Pages)** {#chapter-3:-risk-identification-(10---15-pages)}

## **3.1. Risk Identification** {#3.1.-risk-identification}

### **3.1.1. Market Risk** {#3.1.1.-market-risk}

Market risk refers to the uncertainty surrounding customer adoption, user retention, market acceptance, and the long-term sustainability of Mekong Pathfinder in the emerging climate-resilient mobility market. Although urban flooding has become an increasingly severe challenge in the Mekong Delta, the existence of a clear problem does not automatically guarantee widespread adoption of a new digital solution. As an early-stage startup introducing a relatively new category of flood-aware mobility services, Mekong Pathfinder faces uncertainty regarding whether users will consistently recognize, adopt, and remain engaged with its value proposition (Blank & Dorf, 2020; Ries, 2011).

A major market risk is user behavioral inertia. Residents in the Mekong Delta commonly rely on informal information channels, including Facebook groups, Zalo communities, personal networks, and local experience, to obtain updates on flooding and traffic conditions. These alternatives are familiar, easily accessible, and generally free of charge. Consequently, persuading users to change established mobility habits and adopt a dedicated platform may prove challenging despite the potential benefits of safer route recommendations and real-time flood intelligence. Market validation involving 245 respondents indicated encouraging demand, with 73.1% rating the platform as necessary or highly necessary. However, positive attitudes toward an innovation do not necessarily translate into sustained adoption or routine usage behavior (Blank & Dorf, 2020).

Another significant market risk involves user retention and community participation. Because flooding is seasonal, demand for flood-related services may fluctuate throughout the year, creating the possibility of seasonal churn. This challenge is particularly important because Mekong Pathfinder relies in part on community-generated intelligence to strengthen situational awareness and local relevance. Although 62.9% of respondents expressed willingness to contribute community reports and 86.1% indicated conditional willingness to share anonymous location data, actual participation rates may be substantially lower than stated intentions. Insufficient user engagement could weaken network effects, reduce the value of community-generated insights, and slow the development of the platform’s data ecosystem (OECD, 2021; Parker et al., 2016).

Market uncertainty also exists regarding institutional monetization and regional scalability. Because the B2C application is provided free of charge to maximize crowdsourced data generation, the platform's commercial sustainability depends entirely on Business-to-Business (B2B) and Business-to-Government (B2G) enterprise adoption. Although the mobility problem is severe, converting municipal governments and logistics operators into paying subscribers involves long sales cycles, bureaucratic procurement processes, and a high burden of proof for data accuracy. Furthermore, successful pilot deployment in Can Tho does not guarantee equivalent institutional acceptance across other provinces in the Mekong Delta, where smart-city budgets, digital readiness, and flood exposure may differ significantly. These variations may limit expansion opportunities beyond the initial pilot market.

If these market risks are not effectively managed, they may constrain user data acquisition, weaken the crowdsourced network effect, delay institutional commercialization, and ultimately limit the platform’s scalability within the regional GovTech ecosystem.

### **3.1.2. Competition Risk**

Competition risk poses a significant strategic challenge for Mekong Pathfinder due to the dominance of established digital platforms in the mobility and navigation ecosystem. Unlike startups entering an uncontested market, Mekong Pathfinder competes in an environment dominated by strong incumbents such as Google Maps, Waze, and Grab, all of which benefit from extensive user bases, mature digital ecosystems, high brand recognition, and substantial technological resources. These advantages create significant barriers to entry and increase the difficulty of achieving sustainable market positioning (OECD, 2021; Parker et al., 2016).

A major competitive threat arises from the possibility of feature replication. While Mekong Pathfinder differentiates itself through climate-resilient mobility intelligence and flood-aware navigation, large technology companies possess the resources and existing mapping infrastructure to incorporate similar capabilities into their platforms if market demand becomes sufficiently strong. As digital platforms frequently expand by integrating niche innovations, the project's current differentiation may gradually diminish if competitors introduce comparable flood-alert or safety-routing capabilities (Deloitte, 2023; Parker et al., 2016).

Competition risk is further intensified by network effects and ecosystem lock-in. Navigation platforms become increasingly valuable as user participation grows, generating continuous streams of mobility information that improve overall service quality. Because users already rely on existing platforms for navigation, ride-hailing, location search, and related services, switching to a specialized platform may involve behavioral and ecosystem barriers even when alternative solutions offer superior localized functionality. Consequently, incumbent platforms benefit from self-reinforcing advantages that can limit the growth potential of emerging competitors (Parker et al., 2016).

Another competitive challenge involves the sustainability of differentiation. Although Mekong Pathfinder currently focuses on the unique mobility challenges of flood-prone urban environments, maintaining this advantage requires the continuous development of specialized local capabilities. The platform's long-term competitiveness depends on establishing a defensible local ecosystem based on community participation, localized hazard intelligence, and hyper-local mobility services. From a competitive perspective, failure to develop these localized assets may weaken barriers to imitation and reduce strategic distinctiveness. The continuity and management of such data assets are discussed separately in Section 3.1.4 Data Risk (OECD, 2021).

Furthermore, competition may emerge not only from navigation providers but also from alternative smart-city, weather-information, and disaster-management platforms that increasingly deliver mobility-related services. As digital transformation accelerates, multiple stakeholders may seek to occupy the same urban-intelligence space that Mekong Pathfinder targets (World Bank, 2023; Deloitte, 2023).

If these competitive pressures are not effectively addressed, Mekong Pathfinder may experience reduced differentiation, slower market penetration, weaker ecosystem positioning, and greater difficulty achieving long-term scalability and commercialization within the Mekong Delta smart mobility sector.

### **3.1.3. Technical Risk**

Technical risk represents one of the most critical risk categories for Mekong Pathfinder because the platform's core value proposition depends on the reliability, accuracy, and real-time performance of multiple interconnected technologies. As an AI-first mobility intelligence platform, the system relies on computer vision, geospatial analytics, routing algorithms, cloud processing, and mobile service delivery to generate timely, flood-aware mobility recommendations. Consequently, technical failures may directly affect service effectiveness, operational continuity, and user confidence in the platform's outputs (Belcastro et al., 2025).

A primary technical risk arises from the limitations of AI-powered flood detection and environmental interpretation. The Virtual Flood Sensor framework relies on computer vision models to detect flood conditions using visual data. However, variations in lighting conditions, camera positioning, visual obstructions, and rapidly changing urban environments may reduce model performance and increase prediction uncertainty (Jafari et al., 2021; He et al., 2024). In particular, false-positive predictions may incorrectly classify roads as hazardous, reducing routing efficiency, while false-negative predictions may fail to identify actual flood risks, potentially compromising the reliability of mobility recommendations. Because Mekong Pathfinder supports safety-related travel decisions, prediction errors may have consequences that extend beyond ordinary software inaccuracies.

Another significant technical risk stems from the complexity of system integration. Mekong Pathfinder combines AI inference, GIS-based routing, community intelligence services, cloud infrastructure, and mobile applications into a single ecosystem. The high degree of interdependence among these components increases the possibility that failures in one subsystem may propagate across the platform, reducing overall system reliability and service quality (Belcastro et al., 2025).

The platform also faces risks related to scalability, system availability, and real-time responsiveness. As user adoption grows and larger volumes of images, routing requests, and mobility data are processed simultaneously, maintaining low-latency performance becomes increasingly challenging. Service interruptions, delayed updates, or reduced processing efficiency during peak demand may undermine user trust and diminish the platform's practical value in critical mobility situations (McKinsey & Company, 2021).

Furthermore, AI-driven platforms face the risk of technological obsolescence and model drift. Changes in urban infrastructure, traffic patterns, and flood characteristics may gradually reduce the predictive effectiveness of previously trained models. Continuous advancements in artificial intelligence technologies may also increase performance expectations across the industry, creating pressure for ongoing adaptation and optimization (OECD, 2021).

Given that Mekong Pathfinder operates as an AI-enabled decision-support platform for flood-prone mobility environments, technical risk directly influences service reliability, operational continuity, public trust, and the platform's long-term viability as a smart-city mobility solution.

### **3.1.4. Data Risk**

Data risk represents a critical challenge for Mekong Pathfinder because the platform operates as a data-intensive urban mobility intelligence system whose value is fundamentally determined by the quality and reliability of its underlying data ecosystem. The platform relies on multiple data sources, including camera feeds, community-generated reports, traffic information, and geospatial datasets, to generate localized flood intelligence and mobility insights. Consequently, weaknesses in data quality, availability, continuity, or representativeness can directly reduce the usefulness of the platform's decision-support capabilities (OECD, 2021; Deloitte, 2023).

One of the most significant risks relates to data quality, reliability, and veracity. Mekong Pathfinder integrates information from heterogeneous sources that may vary considerably in accuracy and consistency.
